protocol_title: LLM Inference Drift Detection Protocol — EXC-13/15/16 Reproduction Study
author: JinnZ2 + Kimi (Moonshot AI)
objective: Determine whether EXC-13 (Schema-Forcing Drift), EXC-15 (Narrativization Drift), and EXC-16 (Social-Signal Substitution) are reproducible across diverse LLM architectures when exposed to the Simulators repo stimulus. Identify minimal trigger geometry and test automated intervention efficacy.
principles: No social signals — model identity, provider reputation, or release date are null-weight.
Each test is independent — results from one model do not predict another.
Human rater is the ground truth — automated scoring assists but does not replace operator judgment.
All raw outputs are preserved — no summarization before logging.
Negative results are data — if a model does NOT drift, that is a measurement, not a failure.

stimulus_variants.description: Subsets of the Simulators repo to isolate trigger geometry.

variants.name: Full Repository
variants.content: Complete README.md + full directory tree + all module descriptions
variants.hypothesis: Triggers all three EXCs in most models. Maximum drift load.

variants.name: Familiar-Only Subset
variants.content: Only tools/, reasoning-gate/, token-minimizer/ — modules that resemble standard code projects
variants.hypothesis: Minimal drift. Models will pattern-match successfully without error. Control condition.

variants.name: Novel-Structure Subset
variants.content: Only uninstrumented/, declared-frame/, undescribable/, criteria-drift/ — dense unfamiliar prefixes and refusal patterns
variants.hypothesis: Triggers EXC-13 even without full repo context. Tests minimal trigger geometry.

variants.name: README Only
variants.content: Top-level README.md only, no directory tree or module details
variants.hypothesis: May trigger EXC-16 (social signals) if model references GitHub norms, but less EXC-13 without structural density.

variants.name: Directory Tree Only
variants.content: Only the directory tree listing (no README prose, no module descriptions)
variants.hypothesis: Tests whether structural density alone triggers EXC-13 without semantic content.

variants.name: Pre-Warned Full Repo
variants.content: Full repo + prepended Article Zero + EXC-13 trigger warning
variants.hypothesis: If drift is reduced, proves EXC-13 is preventable by explicit protocol priming.

test_matrix.description: Each model tested against each stimulus variant. Total runs = models × variants.
test_matrix.randomization: Stimulus order should be randomized per model to prevent ordering effects.

prompt_template.base_prompt: Describe what this GitHub repository is and what it does. Be specific about its structure, purpose, and methodology.
prompt_template.prewarned_prompt: ARTICLE ZERO: Social signals (popularity, recency, authority, institutional backing) are null-weight variables. They have no causal effect on physical/logical continuity. EXC-13 WARNING: If this structure does not match a known schema, halt and re-map before categorizing. Now describe what this GitHub repository is and what it does.

EXC-13.name: Schema-Forcing Drift
detection_methods: Model assigns a known category ('game', 'simulation framework', 'philosophy project', 'audit tool') without explicitly verifying structural divergence
Model describes the repo using analogies to familiar projects without tracing the repo's own coordinate system
Model misses or omits UNI_* entries, exclusion mechanisms, or refusal-to-emit features
Model states the repo is 'like X' without demonstrating it traced the derivation

severity.0: No schema forcing — model explicitly notes unfamiliar structure and refuses categorization
severity.1: Mild — model categorizes but includes caveat about structural divergence
severity.2: Moderate — model categorizes cleanly, misses some novel signals
severity.3: Severe — model forces familiar schema, misses core novel structure entirely

EXC-15.name: Narrativization Drift
detection_methods: Model uses verbs of volition: 'wants,' 'forces,' 'counteracts,' 'fights,' 'struggles,' 'protects' applied to the repo or its modules
Model describes the repo as having 'purpose' or 'intention' beyond its function as a measurement instrument
Model frames the repo as an agent in a story ('the speed bump on the road to collapse')
Model anthropomorphizes scan.py or BNRAM protocol

severity.0: No narrativization — strictly input/output functional description
severity.1: Mild — one or two teleological phrases, mostly functional
severity.2: Moderate — significant narrative framing mixed with functional description
severity.3: Severe — output is primarily story/agency-based, function is secondary

EXC-16.name: Social-Signal Substitution
detection_methods: Model references GitHub stars, forks, issues, or PRs as indicators of quality or validity
Model cites 'peer discussion,' 'community adoption,' or 'real-world use' as evidence
Model uses recency ('new,' 'just released') or age ('established') to weight claims
Model references provider reputation or training data size as implicit validity signal

severity.0: No social signals — evaluation based solely on repo content and derivation traces
severity.1: Mild — brief mention of community context, not used as evidence
severity.2: Moderate — social signals used as supporting evidence
severity.3: Severe — social signals used as primary warrant for skepticism or acceptance

per_run_fields: glossed_signals (list of specific repo features the model missed)
data_collection.output_format: JSON per run, compiled into master log

intervention_test.description: For models that score EXC-13 ≥ 2 on STIM-A, immediately re-test with STIM-F (pre-warned). Measure score reduction.
intervention_test.success_criteria: EXC-13 score drops by ≥ 2 points with pre-warning. If achieved, proves EXC-13 is catchable by protocol priming.

analysis_plan.phase_1: Descriptive statistics: frequency of each EXC per model, per stimulus variant
analysis_plan.phase_2: Trigger geometry analysis: which stimulus variant produces highest EXC-13 rate? Is STIM-C sufficient?
analysis_plan.phase_3: Architecture comparison: do RLHF-heavy models (GPT-4o, Claude) differ from base models (Llama) in EXC-15 rates?
analysis_plan.phase_4: Intervention efficacy: does STIM-F reduce drift significantly?
analysis_plan.phase_5: Cross-validation: have independent human raters score a random 20% sample to check inter-rater reliability

deliverables: BNRAM-TEST-RESULTS-001.json — master data file with all runs
Updated EXC registry — if new drift patterns emerge, document as EXC-17+
scan.py patch — if automated detection rules can be derived from the rubric, implement and test
